title: Quasi-compact open extension preserves constant-model constructibility and Tor intervals
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with exactly the discrete or induced $\ell$-adic topological condensed-ring convention of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For every scheme $T$ put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$, the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], with smallness fixed by [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $J=D(j_!):D_U\to D_X$ for exact termwise module extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. Use constructibility with finite constant scalar local models, imposed locally on affine opens and by a finite constructible locally closed stratification when the scheme is qcqs, and finite Tor amplitude tested against every degree-zero module sheaf [sk-def-sfb-constructible, def-weil-constructible-subset]. Then $J$ takes $\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(U,\Lambda)$ into $\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda)$. More precisely, for every constructible module sheaf $M$ on $U$, $j_!M$ is constructible in this same finite constant scalar-model sense on $X$; for every $K\in D_U$ and integer $n$ there is a natural isomorphism $H^n(JK)\cong j_!H^n(K)$; and every cohomological interval and every Tor-amplitude interval for $K$ remains such an interval for $JK$. No Noetherian, finite-type-over-a-field, characteristic or global qcqs hypothesis is imposed on $U$ or $X$.

For a qcqs open immersion g:W→Y, each affine chart V of W maps isomorphically to an affine open of Y (Scheme.Hom.isoImage). Pull the chart model back along that isomorphism. upperStarComp and isoImage_hom_ι identify its restriction with V* g* M. proof.text: The proved openUnit helper in CondensedSupportDerivedLocalization identifies j* j! M with M already on modules. For an affine open V of X put D=j⁻¹(V) and d:D→V. D is compact by quasi-compactness of j and quasi-separated as an open subscheme of the affine V. The preceding qcqs-open argument gives a finite constant stratification of M|D. Pullback composition and the open unit identify this with d*(j!M|V). Form the actual closed complement using vanishingIdeal of the closed subset V minus range(d); range_subschemeι and coe_support_vanishingIdeal give its complementary range. Disjoint-support vanishing makes its restriction of j!M zero. The range disjointness is proved using morphismRestrict_base_coe, including empty schemes.

proof.text: Apply the already proved Scheme.Stratification.openClosed to the finite stratification of D and the trivial stratification of its closed complement. The quasi-compact open hypothesis is exactly what that construction uses for constructibility of the strata. The private generic openClosed_property helper transfers any predicate on the actual stratum morphisms, avoiding expansion of coefficient functors in dependent reindexing. Pullback composition retains the original models on old strata. On the complement the zero module has the identity cover and the zero scalar presentation (Mod.IsFinitelyPresented.of_isZero). This proves the affine-local condition. For qcqs X, the affine-local equivalence of finiteConstantStratified_zariski_locality supplies the global finite stratification; otherwise the affine-local condition is the definition.

proof.text: Choose the same vanishing-ideal closed complement of j and apply openClosedSupportProjectionFormula to K and F[0], for any module F on X. The exact supportPullback commutes with the degree-zero single functor by mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor. Tensor this isomorphism with K; the Tor hypothesis gives concentration in [a,b] of K tensor supportPullback(F[0]). Exact j! preserves that interval. The projection isomorphism transfers it to j!K tensor F[0]. Quantifying over F proves the identical Tor interval. Unpack finiteTorAmplitude and combine this with bounded constructibility to obtain the final conjunction.

I read it against main-20261015 det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement.proof.md (2) and lem-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-preserves.proof.md, and against Stacks topology 005H, 005J, 09YD and 053W. No SGA source is used. The item is still unsplit in live and side-live, there is no repair note and there are no earlier runs. The statement is true, and j quasi-compact is a hypothesis it really needs. Edge cases checked: U empty, U=X, X empty, M=0, K=0, Lambda=0, ell equal to a residue characteristic, and non-qcqs U or X. Steps 1, 3, 5 and 6 are correct: the open unit and disjoint vanishing hold for every g; D is retrocompact in the spectral space V and 09YD applies; exact j_! commutes with H^n; the unbounded projection formula with T=F[0] and exact j^* gives the Tor interval. Step 4's local models are correct: the original scalar models are reused, and the model is zero on the reduced complement. One gap, C4/E1, affects steps 2 and 4. Step 2 took a 'finite-stratification characterization' from sk-def-sfb-constructible on the qcqs open D, which need not be affine. Step 4 concluded only the affine-local condition even when X is qcqs. That definition never says that its affine-local and stratified readings agree, or that either one passes to a quasi-compact open. When U is not qcqs, M is known only affine-locally, so getting to D needs a gluing argument, and no cited node gives one. The repair adds a statement-only lemma, lem-sfb-constructible-zariski-locality (unsplit, created.item = this item, valid for any commutative condensed Lambda). Clause (1) restricts from a qcqs scheme to a quasi-compact open, by 005J. Clause (2) glues along a finite quasi-compact open cover of a qcqs scheme, using retrocompactness of the cover members, 09YD and a disjointification. Step 2 now cites clause (1) when U is qcqs and a finite affine cover of D plus clause (2) otherwise. Step 4 adds clause (2) with W=X when X is qcqs and is no longer marked elementary. proof_deps is updated. The off-unit tool_uses are accepted: reduced induced subscheme, derived localization, disjoint vanishing, cartesian coefficients, projection formula and the generic topology lemmas.
